gaps.sentence: My laptop, ___ I bought only last year, has already crashed twice.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clause about a thing: 'which', never 'that'.

gaps.sentence: Our new neighbours, ___ have three children, moved in last week.
gaps.hint: people as subject; clause between commas
gaps.explanation: 'Who' is used for people in non-defining clauses; 'which' is for things.

gaps.sentence: The shower suddenly stopped working, ___ meant we had to call a plumber.
gaps.hint: refers back to the whole event
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to the whole preceding clause; 'what' cannot introduce this kind of clause after a comma.

gaps.sentence: Have you got anything ___ will remove this stain?
gaps.explanation: After 'anything', 'that' is the preferred relative pronoun; 'which' is avoided after -thing words.

gaps.sentence: They chose a guide on ___ they could rely completely.
gaps.hint: rely on somebody — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: After the preposition 'on', the person takes 'whom'; 'which' is only for things.

gaps.sentence: Students ___ hand in their essays late will lose marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to the students performing the action; the verb 'will lose' follows later in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: The lawyers, against ___ the case was brought, denied everything.
gaps.hint: the case was brought against them
gaps.explanation: 'Against whom' is the formal relative pattern; 'who' and 'that' cannot follow prepositions.

gaps.sentence: This is the beach ___ we used to play as children.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' introduces place information; 'we used to play' already has a subject and object, so 'which' is impossible.
